full_judgment:
2. Briefly, the facts of the case is that the petitioner Rupali Bank Limited represented by his Thana Road Branch, Bogra, instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 326 of 1994 against the opposite parties in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Bogra for realization of Taka 17,07,996.30 including interest on 30-9-1994 by sale of mortgaged properties described in the schedule of the plaint contending inter alia, that the defendant No. 1 being a businessman, used to deal with electronics goods filed an application to the plaintiff's bank to renew his previous loan, thereafter, on 11-6-1988 vide sanction letters Nos. 45 and 46 the bank sanctioned loan for an amount of Taka 2,00,000 as cash credit hypothecation and Taka 10,00,000 as cash credit total of Taka 12,00,000 in favour of the defendant: The defendant No. 2 became guarantor of the said loan and mortgaged his property mentioned in the scheduled of the plaint with the bank by a registered deed. In the sanction letter it was stipulated that the defendant would repay the loan money with the stipulated. time, but since he failed to repay the loan amount till 30-9-1994 the cash credit hypothecation amount stood Taka 5,19,331 and cash credit pledge amount stood at Taka 11,88,665.30 in all the amount of loan stood at Taka 17,07,996. On 11-8-1993 the Bank through its legal adviser served notice to repay the loan amount within 15 days, although the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 received the same but refused to pay the loan amount verbally and the defendant No. 2 also did not agree to pay the loan obtained by the defendant No. 1. Hence, the suit for realization of money by the plaintiff bank. 

 3. The suit was contested by the defendant-respondents opposite parties by filing written statements denying all the averments made in the plaint contending inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable due to barred by limitation, waiver, acquiescence, estoppels and for want of jurisdiction. Their case is that the defendants received Taka 2,00,000 as cash credit hypothecation loan and Taka 6,00,000 as pledge loan from the bank and, thereafter, on 3-3-1997 the defendant No.1 withdrew Taka 2,00,000 and, thereafter, again withdrew Taka 2,00,000 on 21-3-1987 as cash credit pledge loan and withdrew Taka 4,00,000 by a cheque. Thereafter, upon an application of the defendant the loan amount was increased from Taka 6,00,000 to Tak 10,00,000 and the said loan was renewed. The defendant by the said money purchased goods and kept those in a showroom and in a godown under the supervision and control of the bank. Thereafter, on 30-5-1988 the defendant repaid the entire amount of loan under pledge with interest and on 5-6-1988 he made payment of cash credit hypothecation loan to the bank. Thereafter, on 11-6-1988 the defendant upon an application received Taka 2,00,000 as cash credit hypothecation and Taka 10,00,000 as cash credit pledge loan, in all Taka 12,00,000 vide two sanction letters being Nos. 45 and 46. The defendant purchased goods and kept those in a godown under control and supervision of the bank. On different dates the defendant sold the goods from the godown with the permission of the bank and deposited the sale proceed with the bank. Thereafter, on 15-12-1988 the period of renewal of the loan expired, the plaintiff asked the defendant No. 1 to renew the loan facility. Up to 9-4-1998 there was an outstanding dues of Taka 7,68,729.80 against the defendant No.1 under cash credit pledge and Taka 1,97,997 under cash credit hypothecation. The defendant No.1 deposited Taka 2,96,100 to the bank, but subsequently without giving any notice the plaintiff bank suddenly locked the shop of the defendant No. 1 . As a result the defendant No.1 could not run his business any more. The shop of the defendant No.1 was not mortgaged to the bank, the defendant time and again applied to the bank to open his shop but failed. Thereafter, on 28-7-1990 the defendant filed an application to the bank, requesting to transform his loan account to a block account at the advice of the Manager of the Bank, but it also went in vain. Subsequently, new Manager came and the defendant filed another application requesting him to open his shop and allow the defendant to run his business. The defendant also requested him to transform the loan account to a block account and also requested to him to sale the goods kept in the godown under the supervision of the bank, and to adjust the same with the outstanding dues. The said application of the defendant was received by the bank on 29-7-1990 and on 31-10-1990 the defendant No. 1 again sent a similar application, but they did not pay any heed to it. Thereafter, in the presence of the manager an audit took place regarding the goods kept in the godown, but it was found that most of the goods were damaged and since the goods were kept under lock and key for quite a long time those were destroyed and became useless. Thereafter, time and again defendant No.1 requested the plaintiff bank to transform the loan account to a block account without interest and prayed for allowing him to pay the loan installment but all his efforts went in vain. The defendant No.1 further stated that on 13-4-1989 his shop and godown were kept under lock and key by the plaintiff bank, as a result lie had to incur a loss of Taka 17,00,000 to Tak 20,00,000 and for this loss the Bank was fully responsible since for the negligence of the plaintiff bank the defendant could not run his business, he could not repay the loan amount in time As such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. To prove the case the plaintiff adduced 1 (one) witnesses as PW 1. The defendant also adduced one witness as DW 1 and both the side cross-examined those witnesses and the parties also exhibited some documentary evidence to prove their respective cases. 

 7. A Division Bench of this court after hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record allowed the said appeal and set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and sent back the case on remand to the trial court for disposal afresh of the suit with some observation by its judgment and order dated 18-5-2011. 

 12. Mr Md Imam Hasan, the learned Advocate along with Md Shahinul Islam, Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner argued that both the courts without considering the material facts of the case erroneously passed the impugned judgment without including the interest. He further submits that the courts below though found that the defendant failed to prove their case about their loss of business as claimed whereas the courts below without considering the provision of law passed the impugned judgment. He submits that ignoring the provision of law the courts below deducting the deposited amount from the decreetal amount without measuring the rate of interest. He further submits that as per provision of section 50 of Artha Rin Adalat Am the plaintiff is entitled to get decree and fixed the rate of interest provided under sub-section 2 of section 50 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and the court has no authority to reduce the said interest fixed in the Artha Rin Adalat Ain as such the impugned judgment passed by the courts below should be interfered with. He further submits that the courts below though observed that the defendant No.1 failed to produce documents and accordingly did not consider the damage as claimed by the defendant whereas observed that the bank did not give permission to sale of pledge goods for long 20 years and due to such action of the Bank earning source of the defendant was closed which is self contradictory finding as such the impugned judgment of the courts below are liable to be interfered with. He prayed for making the Rule absolute. 

 13. Mr Md Zahedul Bari, the learned Advocate along with Ms Nazmun Nahar, Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties argued that the trial court as well as the appellate court after proper consideration of the evidence on record passed the impugned judgment. He further submits that though the courts below did not consider the damage and loss of the business of the opposite parties but inadvertently the defendant opposite party did not prefer appeal as such the defendant is not entitle to get the same. He further submits that the trial court after considering the observation made by this Hon'ble court passed the impugned judgment which need not be interfered with. He further submits that earlier a Division Bench of this court sent back the suit to the trial court directed the trial court to keep in the mind that the plaintiff bank did not convert the account of the defendant No. 1 as the block account ignoring the recommendation of the higher authority. The shop and the godown of the defendant was illegally kept under lock and key for 10 to 12 years as a result defendant had to incur a huge financial loss and the plaintiff bank is liable for such losses of the defendant, which should be assessed and deducted from the total amount of the decree and considering the said observation the trial court took view that the plaintiff is not entitled to get any further interest as provided under sub-section 2 of section 50 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. He further submits that after the decree of the trial court the defendant deposited all the decreetal amounts but the plaintiff bank since did not receipt the said decreetal amount the defendant deposited the same to the Artha Rin Adalat Bogra and no installment is remained since enter decreetal amount has been deposited to the court by the defendant opposite party. He further submits that both the courts after proper consideration of the evidence on record and the findings of this court properly adjudicated the case and passed the impugned judgment which should not be interfered with. He prayed for discharging the Rule. 

 14. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the impugned judgment of the courts below, the papers and documents is available on the record and the judgment passed by a Division Bench of this court. This is a suit for realization of lone money by plaintiff bank. Initially the trial court dismissed the suit and against which the plaintiff bank preferred First Appeal No. 635 of 2002 before this court and a Division Bench of this Court after consideration of the evidence on record allowed the said appeal on setting-aside and judgment of the trial court and sending back the case on remand to dispose of the suit afresh with some observations. 

 16. Mr Md Imam Hasan, the learned advocate annexed the said judgment of the High Court Division through supplementary affidavit. It also appears from supplementary affidavit that the defendant-opposite party claimed that the entire decreetal amount has been paid. It appears that Division Bench of this Court on hearing the First Appeal No. 635 of 2000 on 18-5-2011 allowed the appeal and sending back the case on remand to dispose of the suit afresh with some observation. The said observations of this court is reproduced as below: "Since from the evidence it appears that on 9-4-1989 there was an outstanding dues against the defendants. The value of pledge goods valued at Taka 4,41,719.80 (as per inventory list prepared by the inspection team in presence of the defendant No.1) should have been deducted from the outstanding dues of Taka 6,49,750 and after deduction of the said amount the outstanding dues should have been fixed against the defendant." 

 "(1) Justice would be met if we send the case back on remand to the trial Court to calculate the actual dues receivable by the bank from the defendant No.1 keeping in the mind that the plaintiff bank did not convert the account of the defendant No.1 to a block account ignoring the recommendation of the higher authority. 

 18. Mr Md Imam Hasan, argued that last payment of the defendant opposite party on 30-12-1991 and suit was filed on 28-11-1994 which proves that the plaintiff filed the suit within 3 (three) years so no question of barred by limitation in the instant case. The trial court though consider the aforesaid finding of the higher court but did not consider the matter that whether the suit is barred by limitation or not but the trial court decreed the suit-in-part. We have considered the material facts and it is found that the last payment by the defendant on 30-12-1991 and the suit was filed on 28-11-1994 which proves that the plaintiff filed the suit within 3 (three) years as per provision of law so no question of barred by limitation in the instant suit. 

 23. Consider the aforesaid findings of the trial court it is our view that the trial court after proper consider of the facts and evidence of the case rightly opined that the plaintiff is not entitled to get interest as per provision of law. The appellate court also took the some view. In such circumstance of the facts we are not inclined to interfere with the said findings about the interest as claimed by the Bank. 

 25. So, considering the aforesaid facts it is our view that court has option not impose the interest as provided under sub-section 2 of section 50 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, since a division bench of this court considering the entire material facts of the case sending back the case on remand to dispose of the suit afresh with some observation and the trial court as well as the appellate court after perusal of the facts of the case passed the impugned judgment which need not be interfered with. 

 26. Now it is well settle principle that concurrent findings of facts cannot be interfered with in revisional jurisdiction provided under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure if no misreading or miscarriage or misappropriation of the facts of the case. This principle settled in the case of Abdul Gafur vs Md Abdur Razzak, reported in 62 DLR (AD) 242 and the case of Shambhu Nath Poddar vs Bangladesh Railway reported in 43 DLR (AD) 82. 

 27. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstance of the case and the discussions as made above, we find no merit in the Rule.
